Question B-006-010-007.

Why the correct answer is right: An elevated quarter-wave vertical is matched to 50-ohm coax by using quarter-wave radials that slope downward. The slope moves the feedpoint impedance close to the coax value.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Horizontal quarter-wave radials": Horizontal quarter-wave radials leave the feedpoint closer to the lower ground-plane impedance, roughly in the 30-ohm range, instead of raising it toward 50 ohms.
- sourceIndex 2: "Horizontal half-wave radials": The radial length is wrong for the quarter-wave ground-plane system, and keeping them horizontal does not provide the 50-ohm impedance shift.
- sourceIndex 3: "Upward sloping half-wave radials": Both parts are wrong: half-wave radials are not the quarter-wave counterpoise called for, and upward slope would not give the desired 50-ohm match.
